findings.claim: Initializing `env` to `{}` is an unsafe default for the generic type `E['Bindings']`, which may be a concrete non-empty binding type.
findings.rationale: `E['Bindings']` is resolved from the user's Env generic (e.g. `{ COUNTER: DurableObjectNamespace }`). `{}` is not structurally assignable to such a type, so this either requires a cast/`as unknown as` to compile or silently lies about the runtime shape: `c.env.COUNTER` is typed as present but is `undefined`. Previously the field was simply uninitialized, which was equally undefined at runtime but at least didn't claim a valid value existed. Fairly confident this is a typing concern; whether it compiles depends on the declared constraint on `Bindings`.

findings.claim: The `{}` default is likely clobbered back to `undefined` by the constructor when `options` is provided but `options.env` is not.
findings.rationale: Context's constructor typically does `if (options) { this.env = options.env; ... }` unconditionally. Class field initializers run before the constructor body, so for any Context created with an options object lacking `env` (a very common path in tests and in non-workers runtimes), `this.env` is reassigned to `undefined` and the new default never takes effect. If the intent is a guaranteed non-null `env`, the assignment needs to be guarded (e.g. `if (options.env) this.env = options.env`). Confidence is moderate since the constructor isn't shown in this hunk — worth verifying.

findings.claim: Behavior change: `c.env` is now truthy/non-null by default, breaking existing `if (!c.env)` / `c.env ?? fallback` guards in user and middleware code.
findings.rationale: Callers commonly branch on whether bindings exist (e.g. to distinguish Workers from Node/Deno runtimes, or to fall back to `process.env`). With a `{}` default those guards stop firing and property access yields `undefined` deeper in the call chain instead, turning an early, explicit check into a later, less obvious failure. This is a real observable semantic change for existing consumers.

findings.claim: Adding an object-literal field initializer allocates a fresh object on every Context construction, adding per-request overhead.
findings.rationale: A Context is created for every request in a hot path; the previous uninitialized field cost nothing, whereas `= {}` allocates a new empty object per instance even when it is immediately overwritten by `options.env`. In a framework where per-request allocations are deliberately minimized this is a measurable (if small) regression; a shared frozen empty-object constant would avoid it.
